# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This prevents debconf from asking interactive questions during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all necessary dependencies in a single layer to optimize image size.
# This includes build tools, version control, MPI, required libraries for LAMMPS,
# certificates, and libgomp1.
# CORRECTED: Added python3, which is a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake build system.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    python3 \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for running in containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow running MPI applications as the root user and ensure
# that TCP is used for communication between pods, which is standard in K8s.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code from the official repository.
# Build LAMMPS from source using CMake, enabling the required REAXFF, MPI, and OMP packages.
# Finally, copy the main LAMMPS executable 'lmp' to a system-wide location on the PATH.
RUN git clone https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /lammps && \
    cd /lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D BUILD_OMP=yes \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=yes && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' command copies the executable and sets correct permissions.
    install -m 755 lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# As requested, copy the specific example files from the cloned source
# into the final working directory.
RUN cp /lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Set a default command to provide an interactive shell.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a test run of a LAMMPS reaxff simulation
# on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes environment using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the lammps reax experiment MiniCluster.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  # The manifest will be deployed to the default Kubernetes namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Specifies the number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for single-node execution.
  size: 1
  # The total number of application tasks to run. For this test, we run a single task.
  tasks: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator. Strict mode ensures all logs are captured.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes, allowing for log and artifact inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by Flux. This runs a LAMMPS simulation with specific variables.
      # The Flux Operator will wrap this command with `flux run`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is the main workload, not a launcher pod for interactive sessions.
      launcher: false

# Corrected the Kubernetes manifest to address a previous ErrImagePull failure.
# The primary issue was an inability to pull the arm64 version of the application container.
# FIX: Switched from an ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) to a powerful AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge)
# to ensure a compatible and available container image is pulled.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster size is 1, ensuring all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # FIX: Adjusted the task count to 48 to match the vCPU count of the new c7a.12xlarge instance.
  tasks: 48

  # Pods will not be deleted after the job finishes, allowing for log and artifact inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator. Strict mode ensures all logs are captured.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # FIX: Removed the `flux` block which specified an ARM architecture and is not needed for amd64.

  # Pod spec modifications for scheduling.
  pod:
    # The nodeSelector ensures the pod lands on the specified AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # FIX: Updated the command to partition the 48 tasks across the simulation grid (4*4*3=48).
      command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This container is the main workload, not a launcher pod for interactive sessions.
      launcher: false

The previous run on a 64-core ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) established a strong baseline FOM of 296.365. This attempt will test a modern, compute-optimized 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) to evaluate if its different architecture and potentially higher per-core performance can yield a competitive or better result, despite having fewer cores.

The 64-core ARM HPC instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) yielded the highest FOM of 296.365. The subsequent attempt on a 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) resulted in a lower FOM of 287.546, indicating that for this workload, maximizing core count is the most effective optimization strategy. The hpc7g.16xlarge configuration is therefore considered optimal among the available choices.
